```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  width = 78
)
```

The package reports typed conditions for three common situations: registry
selection, changed information-release pages or attachments, and unavailable
official network resources. The checks below distinguish these cases without
matching complete message text.

## Check the installed registry first

An unknown release ID fails locally before any network request.  Inspect the
registry and use one of its `release_id` values:

```{r unknown-release}
unknown <- tryCatch(
  statsnzreleases::statsnz_latest_release("nz_stats_not_real"),
  error = identity
)
c(class = class(unknown)[[1L]], message = conditionMessage(unknown))
```

Use `include_unsupported = FALSE` to present only the families that the current
package version can pass to `read_statsnz_release()`. The full registry retains
deferred families for visibility and planning.

## Check a page before reading it

An explicit `release_url` must be an official Stats NZ information-release URL,
and the page title must match the selected release family.  When a page is
updated or a wrong family is supplied, inspect its attachments first:

```{r files-live}
if (interactive()) {
  files <- statsnzreleases::statsnz_release_files(
    paste0(
      "https://www.stats.govt.nz/information-releases/",
      "gross-domestic-product-march-2026-quarter/"
    )
  )
  files[, c("name", "title", "extension", "url")]
}
```

Useful typed failures include `statsnz_release_mismatch` (the page belongs to
another family), `statsnz_attachments_not_found` (no downloadable files were
detected), and `statsnz_attachment_mismatch` (the page has files, but none
matches the family rule).  These indicate a source-layout change or an
incorrect URL rather than a parsing problem.

## Network and cache checks

Calendar discovery and attachment reads need access to official HTTPS URLs.
The package uses bounded request timeouts and does not require credentials.  A
request failure is reported as `statsnz_request_error`, an HTTP response outside
the 2xx range as `statsnz_http_error`, and an attachment download failure as
`statsnz_download_error`.

```{r cache}
cache <- statsnzreleases::statsnz_cache_dir()
basename(cache)
```

Pass the same `cache_dir` to later reads to reuse a non-empty downloaded file.
Use `refresh = TRUE` only when you intentionally want to retrieve the
attachment again.  Do not place credentials in a URL or commit cache files;
the cache contains downloaded source files and is managed outside the package
source tree by default.

## Validate an imported object

`statsnz_provenance()` checks that its input carries the package's provenance
attribute.  This catches accidental loss of metadata when a result is copied
into a different object:

```{r provenance-error}
missing_provenance <- tryCatch(
  statsnzreleases::statsnz_provenance(tibble::tibble(value = 1)),
  error = identity
)
c(
  class = class(missing_provenance)[[1L]],
  message = conditionMessage(missing_provenance)
)
```

When `read_statsnz_release()` applies its `series`, `start_period`, or
`end_period` filters, the package preserves provenance on the result.  If a
downstream transformation drops attributes, retain the original object or save
`statsnz_provenance()` before transforming it.

## A reproducible support request

When reporting a failure, include the package version, R version, release ID,
explicit page URL (if used), date/time, and the typed error class.  Do not
include private cache contents or credentials.  Email support requests to <mailto:chartwellmacro@gmail.com>.
